Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old male with approximately 3 days of profuse watery diarrhea, crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting (notably after milk), feverish sensation, and reduced oral intake, consistent with acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk; plan includes oral rehydration and supportive care with return visit if not improved in 48 hours.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Several days of watery diarrhea described as “loads” of stools, very watery and lacking solidity; associated crampy abdominal pain; episodes of nausea and vomiting (notably after milk); feels hot; not sleeping well.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began about 3 days ago ( Monday/Tuesday ).
- Course: Diarrhea occurring roughly every hour when awake; continues to pass fluids; attempting to drink fluids but feels they “go straight through.” Had lunch today with loose stools afterward. Vomited once after consuming milk. Pain is intermittent, midline/central lower abdomen, 6/10 on a pain scale when present. Feverish sensation reported; temperature not measured.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Milk ingestion associated with vomiting; fluids are being consumed but stool output remains high.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, feverish sensation; pain persists intermittently. Urine output described as decreased but present.
- Exposures/contacts: Brother has had similar symptoms for about five days; no clear trigger identified. Family history notable for father with colon cancer.
- Diet/fluids: Drinking water, Diarolyte recommended; solid intake limited with symptoms; had some lunch today with loose stools afterward.
- Sleep: Patient reports not sleeping well.
- Medical history: Patient reports being otherwise fit and well; no regular medications; no known drug allergies.
- Medications: Occasional Paracetamol use (dose, route, frequency not documented).
- Social history:
  - Living situation: Lives with sister and mother.
  - Occupation: Office government work in Central London.
  - Smoking: Social smoker.
  - Alcohol: Occasional alcohol use; Fridays more common, generally infrequent.
- Family history: Father with colon cancer (currently in third stage; details limited).

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- No regular medications.
- No known drug allergies.

Medications:
- Paracetamol occasionally; dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Smokes socially; drinks alcohol occasionally (usually weekends, variable frequency).
- Works in an office setting in Central London.
- Lives with mother and sister.

Family History:
- Father with colon cancer; currently described as in third stage; details limited.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- None reported.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk.
  - Plan:
    - Start or continue oral rehydration with Diarolyte (OTC); ensure adequate fluid intake.
    - Clear fluids preferred; introduce soft diet (soup, mashed foods) and gradually advance as tolerated.
    - Paracetamol as needed for fever or pain; dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Avoid or limit alcohol during illness.
    - Monitor for dehydration; if symptoms do not improve within 48 hours or if dehydration signs develop (e.g., persistent vomiting, reduced urine output, dizziness), contact/return for re-evaluation.
    - No antibiotics prescribed at this time; no investigations ordered unless symptoms persist or worsen.

- Issue 2: Follow-up and return instructions.
  - Plan:
    - Reassess in 1–2 days (around 48 hours) by phone or visit.
    - If dehydration develops or symptoms fail to settle within 48 hours, consider further evaluation.

- General plan:
  - Continue fluids and supportive care.
  - Avoid milk if it appears to trigger vomiting (patient note discussed; advised fluids first).
  - Maintain hydration; monitor intake/output.
  - Encourage Paracetamol as needed for fever/pain.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs and a formal physical examination were not documented; no laboratory tests or stool analyses were performed or ordered; medication dosing for Paracetamol and Diarolyte not recorded; no explicit vaccination or travel history taken.
- Internal conflicts: No explicit contradictions detected in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Audio/dialogue includes some incomplete phrases; occasional interruptions and unclear terms; overall content sufficient to establish probable diagnosis and plan, but lacks objective data (vital signs, physical findings, lab results).
